ysolde_first.title: THE PRICE OF TEA
ysolde_first.text: 'Secrets are the one coin that grows in value,' says Ysolde, stirring tea she will not drink. 'For eight crowns I will tell you who in this room is lying to you. For free, I will tell you to be careful.'

left.label: Say no
left.result: 'Careful, then,' says Ysolde, and pours you a cup you did not ask for.

right.label: Pay her
right.memo: You bought a secret from Ysolde.
branches: She slides a folded note across the table. The steward sells the king's daily plans. To her, and to others.
'The steward? He never sells. I have tried.' It is the nearest thing to praise she gives anyone.

lesson.left: Saying no keeps your hands clean and your purse full. But you stay the one who does not know what everyone else knows.
lesson.right: Bought news is only as good as the seller's reasons. A broker will sell the same true thing to you and to others.

ysolde_ledger.title: THE LONG LIST
ysolde_ledger.text: 'I keep a book,' says Ysolde. 'Your name has grown long in it. Favours, pressure, a few neat lies. Others would pay well to read it. I would much rather be your friend.'

left.label: Buy the page
left.memo: You bought the page in Ysolde's book that had your name.
left.result: The page changes hands. Ysolde keeps a copy, as you would have done.

right.label: Call her bluff
right.memo: You called Ysolde's bluff about the book.
right.result: She shrugs, and for once she looks unsure. Maybe she was bluffing.
branches: Ysolde sells the book to the highest buyer by morning. Every thread leads back to your hand.
A page turns up in the council room. It is not the worst page. It is bad enough.

lesson.left: Paying to keep a record hidden costs less than defending your name. It also keeps the broker in your story.
lesson.right: Daring a record keeper to publish bets that she values her trade more than the sale. Sometimes she does not.

king_ill.title: A FEVER THAT IS NOT A FEVER
king_ill.text: Dr. Aubry shuts the door and does not sit. 'The king's wine, {t}. I have treated many fevers. This is not one. Someone is putting something slow in his cup.'

left.label: Look into it quietly
left.memo: You looked into the king's illness in secret.
left.result: Aubry hands you a small bottle and a list of signs. You tell no one.

right.label: Tell the council
right.memo: You told the council about the poison.
right.result: The council erupts. Everyone looks shocked. Some of them are very good actors.

lesson.left: Staying silent keeps the guilty one comfortable, and comfortable people repeat their habits. You bought time with your own safety.
lesson.right: Telling everyone warns the poisoner as well as the victim. It also makes you the person who raised the alarm.

tasting_cup.title: THE KING'S CUP
tasting_cup.text: At the feast, the king's cup is passed to you. It is a kind gesture and a sign of favour. Aubry's eyes find yours across the table. The wine smells of cloves, and of something under the cloves.

left.label: Let a servant taste it first
left.memo: You had a servant taste the king's cup.
left.result: The servant falls ill within the hour. The cup was bad. The court is shocked, quietly.

right.label: Drink it yourself
branches: Aubry's cure keeps you steady. The court watches someone drink poison and live.
The room tilts. The last thing you see is Aubry running, and nobody else.
You are carried out grey in the face. The cup was bad. You get better in a week. The court tells the story for much longer.

lesson.left: A stand-in keeps your own hands clean, but someone else pays the price, and they did not choose it. People notice who was told to be careful.
lesson.right: Taking the risk yourself shows strong belief. It can also kill you if you do not know what you are drinking.

poisoner_unmasked.title: WHOSE HAND IN THE CELLAR
text: Aubry has traced the poison to the shop that supplies Master Vask. 'He has a reason. The king's death would give him sole rights to trade. He has the means too. That is not proof. But I would not eat his bread.'
Aubry has traced the poison to Lady Dorne's house. 'Her cook bought the herb, and the cook is terrified. The lady is calm. Either she is innocent, or she is a great actress.'
Aubry has traced the poison to the steward's office. 'Quill's key opened the cellar door that night. Was it for gold or from fear? I cannot say. But it was his key.'

left.label: Arrest the guilty one quietly
left.memo: You had the king's poisoner arrested quietly.
left.result: The arrest happens in the middle of the night. By morning, the guilty one has simply left the court.

right.label: Show the proof to the council
right.memo: You showed the council who the poisoner was.
right.result: The council watches {culprit} being led away. For one afternoon, everyone is on the same side.

lesson.left: A quiet arrest ends the danger but leaves questions. Rumours grow from questions.
lesson.right: A public trial gives you the most right to act. It also teaches the next poisoner what to hide.

anonymous_note.title: A GREY SEAL
anonymous_note.text: A note lies under your door, sealed with grey wax. 'Your rise was no accident. Your fall does not have to be one either. Name a place and a time.' The handwriting belongs to someone who never asks permission.

left.label: Ignore the note
left.result: You burn it. The ash smells faintly of lavender, which is somehow worse.

right.label: Name a place and a time
right.result: A stranger delivers the reply and vanishes down the stairs before you finish reading.

lesson.left: Letting a mystery person come to you keeps the first move. But you are now ignoring a powerful person.
lesson.right: Choosing the time and place of a secret meeting feels like control. It only helps if you know who you are meeting.

veiled_meeting.title: THE CARRIAGE WITH CURTAINS
text: The carriage is waiting at your door this time. 'It was rude not to answer,' says the veiled voice. 'I forgive it once. I can make the council lean your way. All I will ask is a name, when the time comes.'

A carriage with closed curtains waits in the church square. The woman inside never lifts her veil. 'I can make the council lean your way,' she says. 'All I will ever ask is a name, when the time comes.'

left.label: Refuse the helper
left.result: The curtain does not move. The carriage drives off at exactly walking speed.

right.label: Accept her help
right.memo: You accepted the Veiled Patron's help.
right.result: By the next council meeting, three locked doors are open.

lesson.left: Refusing an unknown helper keeps you free. It also makes you a fixed point that someone must now work around.
lesson.right: A helper makes you depend on her, and she depends on you. But only she knows how long the leash is.

veiled_price.title: THE NAME
veiled_price.text: The grey seal again. 'The name I mentioned,' says the veiled voice. 'My grandnephew, a boy of eleven. When the king dies, you will speak for him and for no one else. I have waited a long time to ask.'

left.label: Refuse
left.memo: You refused the Veiled Patron's price.
left.result: Doors close in the order they opened. Her favour was a staircase, and she has taken it away.

right.label: Promise to back the boy
right.memo: You promised to back the Veiled Patron's heir.
right.result: You swear it in the shadow of the church. It is the first thing you cannot take back.

lesson.left: Refusing the price loses what you already gained. It also shows others you can say no to the most powerful person in the room.
lesson.right: The price of free help is shown last. Paying keeps you safe. It also ties your future choices to someone else's plan.

unveiling.title: THE COAT OF ARMS
unveiling.text: The grey carriage passes under your window again, curtains shut. A footman stops to fix a strap. For one breath, the coat of arms on the door is visible. You could follow it.

left.label: Let it go
left.result: The carriage turns the corner. Some mysteries are more useful when left alone.

right.label: Follow the carriage
right.memo: You followed the Veiled Patron's carriage.
right.result: It ends at the private gate of Dowager Duchess Isaura Venn, the king's aunt.
branches: It ends at the Dowager Duchess's private door. Her footman looks straight at you. You have been seen.

lesson.left: Leaving a secret alone keeps you off a powerful person's list. It also keeps you blind to the hand that moves the pieces.
lesson.right: Finding out who a helper is gives you power and a weakness. She will wonder what else you have learned.

sabel_gift.title: A GIFT WITH NO STRINGS
sabel_gift.text: Ambassador Sabel gives you a jewelled star finder and bows deeply. 'A gift from the Southern League. No strings, {t}, only friendship.' The lock on the box is beautifully made, like most traps.

left.label: Refuse the gift
left.result: Sabel bows even lower. Only a very good diplomat is so kind about a refusal.

right.label: Accept it
right.result: It is a lovely thing. You find yourself thinking of it whenever the Ambassador is in the room.

lesson.left: Refusing a gift keeps things clean. It costs a little warmth with someone who offered it to build some.
lesson.right: A gift with "no strings" costs less than most and more than it seems. You owe the favour even if the bill never comes.

sabel_treaty.title: A TREATY BY DAWN
text: 'Sign the trade treaty by dawn,' says Sabel, resting a hand on the star finder he gave you. 'The League is generous but in a hurry.' In the corner, Vask shakes his head slightly. Vask has his own reasons to dislike a rival.
'Sign the trade treaty by dawn,' says Sabel. 'The League is generous but in a hurry.' In the corner, Vask shakes his head slightly. Vask has his own reasons to dislike a rival.

left.label: Sign it now
left.memo: You signed the League's treaty overnight.
branches: Money pours in. Somewhere in the small print is a line that nobody read out loud.
The treaty is exactly what it said it was. Sabel looks truly relieved.

right.label: Wait and check it
right.memo: You waited to check the treaty.
branches: Page nine gives the League a road through the mountain pass. Sabel's charm gets thinner.
The treaty is fair. Sabel is hurt that you doubted him, and not completely wrong to be.

lesson.left: Signing fast rewards the one who set the deadline. Whether it was a mistake depends on what was in the treaty.
lesson.right: Asking for time to read what you sign is a normal right. People in a hurry treat it as an insult. Being rushed is a warning sign.

sabel_betrayal.title: A DOOR, NOT A TREATY
sabel_betrayal.text: League "trade inspectors" are in the mountain pass, and there are a great many of them. Kovane storms in with a map. 'You gave it to them, {t}. They never needed a treaty. They needed a door.'

left.label: Cancel the treaty in public
left.note: Sabel tricked you with the treaty.
left.memo: You cancelled the League's treaty in public.
left.result: You admit the mistake in front of the court and send the Ambassador away. Kovane rides for the pass.

right.label: Say it was all planned
right.note: Sabel tricked you with the treaty.
right.memo: You said the treaty was part of a plan.
right.result: You tell the council it is a trap for the League. Nobody believes it, and a few pretend to.

lesson.left: Owning a mistake early limits the damage. It makes your next words easier to believe.
lesson.right: A bluff that hides your own mistake works until someone checks. Then you have two problems.
